_doc: The weekly scout report: what exists out there that this box is not using. Written by the Claude routine described in docs/models.md and read by src/lib/model-scout.ts. Judgment lives here; facts about which model ids a vendor currently sells are NOT — those are pulled live from each vendor's model-list endpoint at read time, because a list committed to git is out of date the day after it is written. Fit verdicts are likewise computed at read time and never stored here: a verdict depends on what is running and how much disk is free, and both change hourly. They are now computed PER HOST — measured against the machine this console is running on, and against each other host's declared specs in config/hosts/*.json — so a claim in `why` or `notes` that a model does not fit needs to name which machine it means.
_schema: candidates[]: { id, name, kind: local|cloud, capability, why, checkpoint?, provider?, target?, mode?, params?, released?, license?, docs?, paper?, requirement? { vramGb, ramGb, diskGb, basis, estimated }, spec? { paramsB, precision, contextK, kind }, runtimes?, pricing? }. Give `requirement` when the authors published usable numbers; give `spec` otherwise and let estimateFromParams() do the arithmetic with an honest basis string. `runtimes` pins weights to one stack (e.g. ["metal"] for an MLX repo) and MUST be omitted for portable weights, which is most of them — absent means "runs anywhere", and GGUF counts as portable. Verdicts are computed per HOST: name which machine you mean in `why` and `notes`, because BeTenshi (31.8 GB VRAM + 63 GB host RAM) and B5 (one 128 GB unified pool) disagree about a good number of models. upgrades[]: { alias, from, to, why } — a like-for-like repoint of an alias already in ai-router.yaml.

candidates.name: RelayVSR (video super-resolution) — Comfy-Org int8 repack, x2 and x4
candidates.params: not published as a parameter count; the deployable unit is one 5.16 GB int8 DiT plus a 0.13 GB fp32 VAE per scale factor — see `requirement`
candidates.released: kopper/RelayVSR created 2026-10-03; lightx2v/RelayVSR_X2 created 2026-10-29; the Comfy-Org repack created 2026-11-05, last modified 2026-11-11
candidates.license: apache-2.0 and NOT gated on ALL THREE repos — the Comfy-Org repack, and both upstreams it is built from (kopper/RelayVSR and lightx2v/RelayVSR_X2). Verified 23-11. This is the whole reason it outranks the LTX adapter below.

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the Comfy-Org repo listing read 23-11, and the four files sum to usedStorage to the byte (10,582,994,448 B = 10.58 GB), BUT YOU DOWNLOAD HALF THE REPO because it ships two scale factors side by side. THE x2 SET, which is the one that matters here: diffusion_models/relayvsr_x2_lightx2v_int8_convrot.safetensors 5,163,295,248 B + vae/relayvsr_flash_vae_x2_fp32.safetensors 127,759,464 B = 5,291,054,712 B = 5.29 GB. The x4 set is the same size to within a megabyte (5,164,179,952 + 127,759,784 = 5.29 GB). x2 is in `diskGb` because the Video Forge's existing upscale pass is x2 (Real-ESRGAN x2), so x2 is the like-for-like replacement; add 5.29 GB if both are wanted. VRAM is 5.29 x 1.15 runtime overhead = 6.08, rounded to 6.1, NOT MEASURED HERE and an admission-style figure in the sense config/model-meta.json uses for every ComfyUI video alias on this box — the 02-10 bake-off measured whole-card peaks of 28-30 GB for models whose admission figures are 14-16 GB, so a VSR pass over a long clip will want more than 6.1 GB and the honest statement is that nobody has run it. NO QUALITY NUMBER IS CLAIMED AND NONE EXISTS: the authors publish no PSNR, SSIM or LPIPS, the Artificial Analysis video arena does not rank upscalers, and docs/models.md's ranking basis for this lane is adoption and licence — which is exactly where this entry's case is made. Nothing here is measured on either box.

candidates.why: NEW THIS WEEK AND IT DISPLACES THE LTX ADAPTER AT THE TOP OF THIS LANE, on licence, adoption and packaging rather than on a quality figure neither model has. WHAT IT WOULD REPLACE, with a measured number: the Video Forge upscales one film in four with Real-ESRGAN x2, and docs/video-forge.md's 02-10 bake-off timed that at 1103 s for 14 clips — about 80 s a clip, roughly 2.4 hours on a 108-clip film. This is a dedicated diffusion video super-resolution model with an OFFICIAL Comfy-Org workflow template (utility_relayvsr_video_x2_upscale.json, in Comfy-Org/workflow_templates), on a box that runs ComfyUI on :8188. WHY IT OUTRANKS Lightricks/LTX-2.5-22b-IC-LoRA-Pixel-Spatial-Upscaler, point by point, because that entry is still in this file directly below and a reader deserves the comparison rather than two unranked options. LICENCE: apache-2.0 and ungated on all three repos in its chain, against `license: other` (ltx-2.x-community-license) behind a `gated: auto` click-through — the LTX adapter is admitted only by the argument that someone here already accepted those exact terms for the installed base, which is a defensible reading but still a reading. ADOPTION, 30-DAY METRIC SAID AS SUCH: 314,403 downloads in the last 30 days, which is also its all-time total since the repack was created on 05-11, and 253 likes — against the LTX adapter's 13,900 in 30 days and 35,205 all-time. That is 23x on the month. INDEPENDENCE: this runs on its own weights, where the LTX adapter does nothing without the 22B local-ltx-2.5 DiT resident and carries the open question of whether a bf16 IC-LoRA applies to an NVFP4-quantised base. WHERE IT LOSES: it is 5.29 GB against 327 MB, and it is a separate pass over decoded frames rather than another pass over latents the DiT already holds — so the LTX adapter is still the cheaper experiment and is still listed. WHICH MACHINE: BETENSHI ONLY, and for a stack reason rather than a size one. ComfyUI runs on BeTenshi and not on B5, whose only image/video path is the Draw Things CLI that config/hosts/b5.json records as unverified and expected to fail. On B5 the 5.29 GB would vanish into a 128 GB pool and there would be nothing to load it with. `runtimes` is deliberately NOT set: these are plain safetensors in diffusion-single-file form, which is portable, and the thing that pins this to BeTenshi is the absence of ComfyUI on B5, not the weight format — pinning it to cuda would state a hardware fact that is not true. WHAT IS NOT KNOWN: nobody here has run it, there is no published quality comparison against Real-ESRGAN, and the int8 convrot format is a Comfy-Org convention whose speed on sm_120 is unmeasured.

THE FIRST THING TO SAY IS STILL WHAT IT IS NOT. docs/models.md defines this lane as 'interactive, playable video' and says to rank it on 'the authors' fps and latency on a named GPU'. PAN 2 IS NOT PLAYABLE AND PUBLISHES NEITHER NUMBER: it is a 50-step diffusion sampler at 704x1248 and 24 fps producing up to 20 s a run, with CFG 2.5 on every step and one worker holding the full 29B model. So the lane's stated ranking basis cannot be applied, and if 'world' here means a model you can play, this lane is still empty. WHAT IT IS INSTEAD: an ACTION-CONDITIONED world model. It takes a current observation (an optional image plus text) and actions described in text, and simulates the outcome as video — the Generative Latent Prediction architecture from 'Critique of World Models', where a language model writes the next world state as a structured, time-grounded description and a 29B MMDiT renders what the description leaves open. WHAT IT WOULD LET THE OWNER MAKE THAT NEITHER BOX CAN MAKE TODAY: A SHOT THAT ANSWERS 'WHAT HAPPENS IF'. The five video models in ComfyUI (Wan 2.2 TI2V 5B, Wan 2.2 14B, LTX-2.5, HunyuanVideo 1.5, MiniMax H3) all take a prompt or a frame and hallucinate forward; none takes a world state and an action and predicts the consequence, and none can be asked the same question twice with different actions and give comparably different answers. For the Video Forge and Montage that is the difference between generating a shot and simulating a scene. WHY IT IS A CANDIDATE AND NOT A NOTE, ENTIRELY ABOUT LICENCE AND PACKAGING: apache-2.0 and ungated on BOTH repos, where every alternative on the hub's video trending list today is still a MiniMax-H3 derivative — H3-Tiny/MiniMax-H3-Tiny-ComfyUI (new 22-11), hyperflow-h3-flash, Pika-H3-Flex, Open-H3-Regenerate-2K, ReDiverse-MiniMax-H3, the LoRAs and GGUF repacks — and docs/models.md rules that family out because MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 is `license: other` and grants no rights in the USA, EU, UK or South Korea, inherited by everything built on it. ADOPTION, 30-DAY METRIC, AND IT IS THE ONE THING THAT MOVED: the Comfy-Org repack has 20,037 downloads in the last 30 days, which is also its all-time total since 15-11, and 62 likes — against ZERO downloads and 17 likes when this entry was written a week ago. Upstream IFM/PAN2 has 809 in 30 days, 819 all-time and 342 likes. Per docs/models.md 5b that is not evidence of quality either way, and here there is no board to fall back on — but it does retire the 'nobody has even downloaded it' caveat this entry carried. WHICH MACHINE, AND THE TWO ANSWERS ARE OPPOSITE FOR OPPOSITE REASONS. BETENSHI (31.8 GB VRAM beside 63.3 GB host RAM): the stack is here and the memory is marginal — 30.7 GB of a 31.8 GB card on an untested assumption about when ComfyUI frees the text encoder, so `fits alone` at best and `won't fit` if that assumption is wrong. WHAT IS LOST, AND IT IS NOT SMALL: VoiceBench 62.4 against 82.8 and Big Bench Audio 44.3% against 81.8%.
